rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-baʿth means sending or dispatching, as in sending someone as a messenger, and also raising someone from the grave.
rows.anchor: البعث: الإرسال، ومنه بعثه رسولا، وبعثه من قبره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazkiya means purification; a pure soul is called zakiyya.
rows.anchor: والتزكية: التطهير، يقال: نفس زكية، أي طاهرة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-Nafs al-Zakiyya was associated with Muhammad b. ʿAbd Allah b. al-Hasan after reports foretold his death at a place of that name, where he was killed.
rows.anchor: وسمي محمد بن عبد الله بن الحسن بن الحسن النفس الزكية؛ لأخبار ظهرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAziz means powerful and unconquerable; the root sense of might is strength, and as a divine attribute it means capable.
rows.anchor: العزيز: القادر الذي لا يغالب، وأصل العزة القوة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other glosses make al-ʿAziz the one whom nothing can thwart or the impregnable; the commentator says these too mean capable as an attribute of essence.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو القادر الذي لا يمتنع عليه شيء، وقيل: المنيع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hakim can mean all-knowing, an attribute of essence, or one who makes his acts precise, an attribute of action.
rows.anchor: وحكيم: بمعنى عالم من صفة الذات، وبمعنى محكم لأفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining the two patriarchs’ prayer for offspring, the verse turns to their prayer for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لما بين تعالى دعاءهما للذرية بين دعاءهما لنبينا فقال تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested messenger is Muhammad, identified with the report that he is Abraham’s prayer and Jesus’s glad tidings in 61:6.
rows.anchor: هو محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم -؛ ولذلك قال: أنا دعوة إبراهيم،

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وجماعة من أهل العلم
rows.claim: They take “among them” to mean the community mentioned earlier.
rows.anchor: يعني في الأمة التي سبق ذكرها، عن الحسن وقتادة وجماعة من أهل العلم.

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli says the prayer concerns descendants around Mecca; only Muhammad fit the description, unlike the prophets of Israel.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: لأنه دعاء للذرية التي تكون حول مكة فلم يبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From them” is glossed either as from the Muslim community or from the people of Mecca; the prayer asks for a guiding prophet who is one of them.
rows.anchor: من الأمة المسلمة، وقيل: من أهل مكة فدعا بشيئين: نبي يهديهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs recited to them are glossed as God’s proofs or as the Qur’an; the commentator prefers Qur’an because it directly fits recitation.
rows.anchor: حججك، وقيل: هو القرآن، وهو أولى لتعلقه بالتلاوة (ويعلمهم الكتاب)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching the Qur’an explains its laws, proofs of divine unity and justice, and other rulings, while recitation first establishes its inimitability and the messenger’s prophethood; the two clauses are not redundant.
rows.anchor: فبالأول تلاوته ليعلموا أنه معجز، وأنه نبي، وبالثاني: يعلم ما يتضمنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation assigns two different descriptions to the Book: it is written, and it is a proof and argument.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وصف الكتاب بصفتين مختلفتين: الأول: أنه مكتوب، والثاني: أنه حجة وبرهان.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets wisdom as the Sunna.
rows.anchor: (والحكمة) قيل: السنة، عن قتادة. وقيل: المعرفة بالدين

rows.speaker: مالك بن أنس
rows.claim: Malik b. Anas glosses wisdom as religious understanding and jurisprudence in interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعرفة بالدين والفقه في التأويل، عن مالك بن أنس.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says wisdom is knowledge of rulings that can only be learned from a messenger.
rows.anchor: وقيل: العلم بالأحكام التي لا تدرك إلا من جهة الرسول، عن ابن زيد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings make wisdom a quality of the Book itself, describing it as scripture, wisdom, and signs; as knowledge together with practice; or as Qur’anic admonitions and its lawful and forbidden matters.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو صفة الكتاب كأنه وصفه بأنه كتاب، وأنه حكمة، وأنه آيات،

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu al-Qasim and Abu Muslim understand the prayer as asking God to establish them in Islam and describe them that way in the future.
rows.anchor: احكم لنا بالإسلام، وصفنا به في المستقبل، عن أبي القاسم وأبي مسلم.

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Judge rejects that future-description reading as far-fetched because a description already attained would serve no purpose; the text also says this reading is unsound because the description is praise and desirable.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي: وذلك بعيد؛ لأن الموصوف إذا حصل له، فلا فائدة في الصفة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss takes being Muslim as exclusive monotheism and sincerity, worshipping and invoking no lord but God; another takes it broadly as observing all Islamic duties, which the commentator prefers for its generality.
rows.anchor: مسلمين قيل: موحدين مخلصين، لا نعبد إلا إياك، ولا ندعو ربا سواك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From our descendants” means from our children, with min partitive; only some are specified because some descendants will not receive God’s covenant through wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ومن ذريتنا أي ومن أولادنا، و(من) للتبعيض، وخص بعضهم؛ لأنه تعالى أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the descendants meant as the Arabs, since they descend from the two patriarchs.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد به العرب؛ لأنهم من ذريتهما،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umma means a group; here it is Muhammad’s community, as confirmed by the request for a messenger from among them.
rows.anchor: (أمة) جماعة وهم أمة محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بدليل قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being Muslim to God means affirming his unity and submitting to him.
rows.anchor: مسلمين لك) موحدين منقادين لك (وأرنا مناسكنا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Show us our rites” may refer to sight with the eyes or, figuratively, sight with the heart—that is, teach us the rites and places of worship, as al-Zajjaj explains.
rows.anchor: (وأرنا مناسكنا) قيل: هو من رؤية العين، وقيل: من رؤية القلب، أي علمنا مناسكنا

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli defines the rites as what brings one near to God, including sacrificial offerings and other Hajj and ʿUmra acts.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي: هي ما يتقرب به إلى الله سبحانه من الهدي والذبائح،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada lists the rites God showed them: circumambulation, saʿy between Safa and Marwa, standing at Arafat and Muzdalifa, and stoning the pillars.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: فأراهما الله تعالى مناسكهما: الطواف بالبيت، والسعي بين الصفا والمروة،

rows.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد
rows.claim: ʿAta and Mujahid interpret the rites as praises.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مدائحنا، عن عطاء ومجاهد. وقيل: شرائع أبينا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the rites as the religious laws of their forefather Abraham; God answered the prayer and Gabriel taught them on the day of Arafah, asking if they recognized each rite, which gave the place and day their names.
rows.anchor: وبعث - جبريك فعلمهما ذلك في يوم عرفة، فكان يقول في كل شيء: عرفت عرفت؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Turn toward us” means either accept our repentance or enable us to repent; one account says they repented only of minor sins because major sins are impermissible for prophets.
rows.anchor: قيل: تقبل توبتنا، وقيل: وفقنا للتوبة، وإنما تابا من الصغائر؛ لأن الكبائر على الأنبياء لا تجوز،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say they prayed for repentance for their sinful descendants or spoke from humility and praise so people could follow their example.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تجب على ظلمة ذريتنا، وقيل: قالاه على جهة الانقطاع إليه، والتسبيح ليقتدى بهما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tawwab is glossed as one who repeatedly accepts repentance or accepts repentance from grave sins; al-Rahim is gracious to his servants and bestows blessings on them.
rows.anchor: قيل: كثير قبول التوبة مرة بعد أخرى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes the duty to turn humbly to God and ask him for gracious aid and support in religion.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على وجوب الانقطاع إليه تعالى، وطلب اللطف والمعونة في الدين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes parents’ rights even if they are unbelievers: the duty arises from parenthood, and unbelief does not remove it; parental maintenance is obligatory in either case.
rows.anchor: وتدل على وجوب حقهما، وإن كانا كافرين لأنه عام، ولأن وجوب الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When parents share the child’s religion, they are owed filial goodness and respect; maintenance and kind companionship are required whether or not their religion matches.
rows.anchor: قلنا: البر والتعظيم، فأما النفقة والمصاحبة بالمعروف فتجب في الحالين،

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that maintenance is obligatory for close relatives; the Shafiʿi position is that it is not.
rows.anchor: فعند أبي حنيفة تجب، وقال الشافعي: لا تجب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes relatives’ rights, distinguishing them from strangers; the commentator states that maintenance for prohibited-degree kin is due only when they share a religion.
rows.anchor: والآية تدل عليه، فتدل على وجوب حق ذوي القربى لتميزهم من الأجانب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes the rights of orphans and the needy, namely meeting their needs.
rows.anchor: وتدل على وجوب حق اليتامى والمساكين، وهو ما يسد خلتهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can establish the obligation of retaliation, completing the benefit of preserving life for everyone.
rows.anchor: ممكن، فتتكامل فائدة بقاء الحياة في الجميع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic phrase is more concise than the proverb it replaces: its twelve letters convey five meanings, while the proverb has fourteen letters and does not convey them.
rows.anchor: فأما الإيجاز فلأنه مع قلة حروفه يدل على معان خمسة كما بينا مما لا يدل عليه المثل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse avoids the repeated expressions of the proverb, which repel taste and hearing; its words are welcomed by hearts and reach the ear unobstructed.
rows.anchor: المثل يشتمل على ألفاظ مكررة ينفر منها الطبع، ويمجها السمع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s harmonious composition is perceptible, unlike the proverb’s; the passage presents this as another rhetorical advantage.
rows.anchor: وأما حسن التأليف: فلأن الآية مؤلفة من حروف متلائمة تدرك حسيا بخلاف المثل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kutiba means prescribed or made obligatory; its root is writing.
rows.anchor: كتب: فرض، ومنه الصلاة المكتوبة، وأصله من الكتابة، وقد بينا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿruf is what cannot rightly be denied.
rows.anchor: المعروف هو الذي لا يجوز أن ينكر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-wasiyya may be the passive subject governed by kutiba, or a subject whose predicate is li-l-walidayn; in the latter analysis the clause is quoted as “the bequest is for the parents.”
rows.anchor: في رفع (الوصية) وجهان: أحدهما: أنه اسم ما لم يسم فاعله، والعامل فيه (كتب).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idha may be governed by kutiba, meaning the duty applies at illness; al-Zajjaj instead takes the will to be made while healthy, with the words “if death comes to us” introducing its terms.
rows.anchor: والعامل في (إذا) قيل فيه وجهان: أحدهما: (كتب) كأنه قيل: كتب عند المرض.

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm says people used to bequeath to distant relatives for prestige while bypassing close kin, so the verse initially made bequests to those kin obligatory to end the custom.
rows.anchor: منعا لهم عما اعتادوه، عن الأصم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says testators had free disposition of their property but were told not to exceed the named recipients; after the inheritance verse came down, the Prophet said God had assigned each right-holder’s share and there is no bequest for an heir.
rows.anchor: قال، صلى الله عليه وسلم -: إن الله تعالى أعطى كل ذي حق حقه، فلا وصية لوارث.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haqqan may be an accusative verbal noun meaning “truly,” an object meaning the bequest was made a right, or an accusative detached from al-wasiyya.
rows.anchor: حقا نصب على المصدر أي حق ذلك حقا، وقيل: على المفعول أي جعل الوصية حقا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that fasting is better supports the view that fasting while traveling is preferable and defeats those who disagree.
rows.anchor: قول من خالف فيه. ويدل قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about those who can bear the fast shows that capacity exists before the act.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله: (وعلى الذين يطيقونه) على أن الاستطاعة قبل الفعل.

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads Qur’an without hamza wherever the word occurs; the other readers pronounce the hamza, and both are linguistic forms.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وحده القران بغير همز حيث كان، والباقون بالهمز، وهما لغتان.

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads al-yusr and al-ʿusr with gemination; the other readers lighten them, with no difference in meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر اليسر والعسر بالتثقيل فيهما، والباقون بالتخفيف، والمعنى واحد.

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Abu Bakr from ʿAsim geminates the m in wa-li-tukammilu; the others do not, and Abu al-ʿAbbas says akmala and kamala mean the same.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم: (ولتكملوا) بتشديد الميم، والباقون بالتخفيف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transmitted reading has damma on the rāʾ of Ramadan; readings attributed to Mujahid with fatḥa and Hasan with sukūn are not allowed because they lack widely transmitted support.
rows.anchor: وحكى أبو القاسم عن مجاهد بفتح الراء، وروي عن الحسن بسكون الراء، ولا تجوز القراءة بهما؛ لأنه خلاف النقل المستفيض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lunar month is twenty-nine or thirty days; legal month reckonings follow the crescents, except the impotent man’s waiting period, reckoned by a solar year according to the commentator’s school.
rows.anchor: والاعتبار في الشهر في أحكام الشرع بالأهلة إلا في مدة العنين، فعندنا يعتبر سنة شمسية لا قمرية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of shahr means appearing: a report is made public and fame is the emergence of a notorious matter.
rows.anchor: وأصله من الظهور، يقال: شهرت الحديث أظهرته، والشهرة ظهور الأمر في شنعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramad means severe heat, and months were named for the seasons in which they fell; Ramadan coincided with hot weather. Its plural is ramadانات.
rows.anchor: رمضان أصل الرمض شدة الحر، وكانوا يسمون الشهور باسم الأزمنة التي فيها وقعت فوافق رمضان أيام الحر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name is variously said to be one of God’s names (making Ramadan “God’s month”), to refer to stones heated by the sun, or to burning away sins.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا، فقيل: سمي رمضان؛ لأن رمضان اسم من أسماء الله تعالى، كأنه قيل: شهر الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an derives from gathering, as recitation gathers letters.
rows.anchor: والقرآن: أصله الجمع، ومنه سمي القراءة؛ لأنها تجمع الحروف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUsr is difficulty and yusr is its opposite, ease.
rows.anchor: والعسر: الصعوبة، ونقيضه اليسر، وهو السهولة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikmal means completing or bringing something to perfection; takbir means magnification.
rows.anchor: والإكمال من الكمال وهو التمام. والتكبير: التعظيم.

rows.speaker: المجبرة
rows.claim: The commentator rejects the claim that guidance is identical to faith: God describes the Qur’an as guidance.
rows.anchor: فتدل على أن الهدى ليس هو نفس الإيمان كما تزعمه المجبرة؛ لأنه تعالى جعل القرآن هدى.

rows.speaker: أصحاب المعارف
rows.claim: The commentator rejects the claim that knowledge is necessary: if it were necessary, calling the Qur’an guidance would add no benefit.
rows.anchor: وتدل على بطلان قول أصحاب المعارف؛ إذ لو كانت ضرورية لما أفاد وصفه بأنه هدى.

rows.speaker: المجبرة
rows.claim: The ease God wills and hardship he does not will contradict the Mujbira claim that God wills every hardship for his servants.
rows.anchor: وهذا خلاف قولهم، فإنهم يزعمون أنه يريد كل عسر بعباده.

rows.speaker: المجبرة
rows.claim: If God does not will hardship for people, he is even less likely to will imposing what they cannot bear or accomplish.
rows.anchor: لأنه إذا كان لا يريد بهم العسر فلأن لا يريد تكليف ما لا يطاق أولى.

rows.speaker: المجبرة
rows.claim: The commentator rejects their doctrine of created acts because the verse attributes making ease and hardship to the responsible people.
rows.anchor: لأنه أثبت أن لهم فعلا بتعسير وتيسير، وتدل على بطلان قولهم أيضا

rows.speaker: المجبرة
rows.claim: The command to complete the count shows God wills that all complete it, contrary to the Mujbira position.
rows.anchor: فبين أنه أراد من الجميع الإكمال، خلاف قول المجبرة.

rows.speaker: المجبرة
rows.claim: The verse shows God wills gratitude from everyone; the commentator contrasts this with the Mujbira view that God wills neglect, gratitude, and disbelief according to each person’s act.
rows.anchor: أنه أراد من الجميع الشكر، وعندهم أراد الإهمال ممن فعله، والشكر ممن شكره، والكفر ممن كفره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that human welfare can depend on a particular place or time, which is why fasting is assigned to Ramadan.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن المصالح قد تعلق بالمكان؛ والزمان لذلك أوجب صوم شهر رمضان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an was revealed on the Night of Decree; the commentator argues the statement is not merely a report about a past event and cites a past-form expression for a future event as an analogy.
rows.anchor: ولا يقال: إنه خبر عن الماضي؛ لأنه بمنزلة قوله: (ونادى أصحاب الجنة) يعني سينادي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is guidance and evidence, and its meaning is intelligible; the commentator rejects claims that its apparent meaning cannot be known or that interpretation must be referred to an Imam, which would strip it of being guidance.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن القرآن يفهم معناه، فيبطل قول من يخالف فيه، وقال: لا يعرف بظاهره،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The month-long fast is obligatory; all agree that a legally responsible person who witnesses the whole month must fast it, while a child reaching maturity or an unbeliever converting owes only the remaining days.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف أن من شهد جميع الشهر وهو مكلف لزمه الصوم، واتفقوا أن الصبي إذا أدرك

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa requires a person recovering from insanity during the month to fast the entire month; al-Shafiʿi requires only the remaining days.
rows.anchor: فعند أبي حنيفة يلزمه صوم الجميع، وقال الشافعي: لا يلزم إلا ما بقي،

rows.speaker: الفقهاء
rows.claim: Jurists agree that the month is established by crescent sighting or by completing thirty days; the commentator rejects esoteric astronomical calculation as against consensus and an essential religious rule, and calls its adherents unbelievers.
rows.anchor: الفقهاء كلهم على أنه يعتبر رؤية الأهلة، أو يكون بالعدد ثلاثين يوما، فأما الذي تزعمه الباطنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excerpt begins to distinguish evidentiary rules for sighting: fasting is established by one man’s testimony, but the following rule for breaking the fast is cut off.
rows.anchor: في الصوم بشهادة رجل واحد، وفي الفطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsar means prevention, while hasr means confinement; the root sense is detention. Abu ʿUbayda, al-Kisaʾi, and most scholars reserve ihsar for illness or loss of provisions, while al-Farraʾ allows the terms to interchange and al-ʿAbbas and al-Zajjaj reject that usage.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين الإحصار والحصر أن الإحصار المنع بالمرض أو ذهاب النفقة، عن أبي عبيدة والكسائي وأكثر أهل العلم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Halq means shaving the head.
rows.anchor: والحلق: حلق الرأس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hady is the plural of hadiyya, like tamra/tamr; it derives from a gift and here means an offering sent to the House as a rite.
rows.anchor: والهدي: جمع هدية كتمرة وتمر، وأصله من الهدية يقال: أهديت إهداء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma in fa-ma istaysara may be nominative, with an understood “upon him is what is easy,” or accusative, with an understood “offer what is easy.”
rows.anchor: فما استيسر محل (ما) رفع، أي فعليه ما استيسر، وقيل: محله نصب،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وعطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Qatada, and ʿAta explain ihsar as being prevented by fear of an enemy or by illness.
rows.anchor: قيل: منعتم بخوف عدو أو مرض، عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وعطاء.

rows.speaker: مالك بن أنس
rows.claim: Malik b. Anas explains it as being held back by an overpowering captor; the commentator prefers the first explanation, meaning prevented from completing the Hajj rites.
rows.anchor: وقيل: منعكم حابس قاهر عن مالك بن أنس. والأول: الوجه، يعني: منعتم من المضي

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: A sheep is identified as the easiest available offering on the authority of ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, and Qatada; the commentator prefers this because it better fits ease.
rows.anchor: قيل: شاة، عن علي. وابن عباس والحسن وقتادة رضي الله عنهم، وهو الوجه؛

rows.speaker: ابن عمر وعائشة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar and ʿAʾisha identify the offering as a camel or cow.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من الإبل والبقر، عن ابن عمر وعائشة، ولا بد في الكلام من حذف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax omits “you must offer” before the offering so the pilgrim can leave ihram; it also omits “and it is slaughtered,” since merely reaching the place does not release him. After slaughter, the prevented pilgrim shaves.
rows.anchor: وتقديره: فعليكم ما استيسر ليخرج به من الإحرام ولا تحلقوا رءوسكم حتى يبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats “do not shave until the offering reaches its place” as a new, unrelated statement; the commentator rejects it and says the words concern the pilgrim prevented from completing Hajj.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل هو كلام مستأنف، لا تعلق له بالإحصار. والأول أصح.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وعطاء وأبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, ʿAta, and Abu Hanifa with his associates hold that the offering’s place is the sanctuary, where slaughter releases the pilgrim.
rows.anchor: قيل: الحرم، فإذا ذبح به حل، عن ابن عباس والحسن وعطاء وأبي حنيفة وأصحابه.

rows.speaker: مالك بن أنس والشافعي
rows.claim: Malik b. Anas and al-Shafiʿi hold that the offering’s place is wherever the pilgrim is released, the place where he was prevented.
rows.anchor: وقيل: محله حيث يحل، وهو الموضع الذي أحصر فيه، عن مالك بن أنس والشافعي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsar permits a pilgrim to exit ihram before finishing Hajj, since completion of the rite does not depend on the offering reaching its destination.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على أن الإحصار يبيح التحلل قبل تمام الحج؛ لأن تمامه لا يقف

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم
rows.claim: The commentator rejects the Murjiʾa expectation of mercy for one who dies persisting in grave sin, citing Abu al-Qasim and saying it conflicts with the verse.
rows.anchor: وهو خلاف الآية، عن أبي القاسم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also refutes saying “I am absolutely a believer”: if a person knew this with certainty, the promise would not be made conditional on hope, since certainty leaves no role for hope or supposition.
rows.anchor: وتدل على بطلان من يقول: أنا مؤمن مطلقا؛ لأنه لو علم ذلك قطعا لما كان الوعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reason believers hope for mercy is that they do not know whether they will remain faithful and repentant throughout the rest of life.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يعلم أحواله في مستقبل عمره، أيقيم على توبته ودينه أم لا؟

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli says believers hope because they do not know whether they have fulfilled every duty owed to God.
rows.anchor: ومنها: أنهم لا يعلمون أنهم أدوا كل ما يجب عليهم، عن أبي علي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Self-examination reveals one’s shortcomings and produces fear, while reflection on God’s mercy produces hope, leaving the believer between the two.
rows.anchor: يرى تقصيره يخاف، ومتى يفكر في رحمته يرجوه، فيتردد بين الخوف والرجاء.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan takes hope here as a guarantee or promise.
rows.anchor: ومنها: أن الرجاء ههنا على الإيجاب، عن الحسن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hijra is a great act of worship; migration after the conquest by someone tested in faith earns great reward, though not the rank of the early emigrants. The report “no hijra after the conquest” means Mecca had become Muslim territory.
rows.anchor: لا هجرة بعد الفتح؛ لأن مكة صارت دار الإسلام.

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read kathir with th; most other readers have kabir with b, which the commentator prefers because of akbar, 4:2, and the majority reading.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي كثير بالثاء، والباقون بالباء، وهو الاختيار لقوله: أكبر،

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads al-ʿafw with nominative case, meaning what they spend is the surplus; the others read it accusatively, meaning tell them to spend the surplus.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو قل العفو بضم الواو، والباقون بالنصب، ووجه الرفع على معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khamr derives from covering: one covers a vessel, and a khimar is so named because it covers the head.
rows.anchor: الخمر: أصله الستر، خمرت الإناء: غطيته، ومنه يسمى الخمار؛ لأنه يغطي الرأس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysir means gambling; proposed derivations connect it with something won by the arrows, with dividing the camel’s meat into shares, or with ease in arranging the joint purchase, all carried out as a lottery.
rows.anchor: والميسر: القمار، وقيل: أخذ من اليسر، وهو وجوب الشيء لصاحبه، من قولهم: تيسر لي

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim describes a camel divided by ten arrows: seven marked arrows carried known shares and three carried none; winners got the corresponding meat share and paid its price, while those with blank arrows got no meat and paid nothing. Outsiders were called burma, while the players were called aysar.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو مسلم أنهم كانوا يبتاعون جزورا ثم يجيلون القداح عشرة، لسبعة منها أنصباء معروفة،

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr says they divided the camel into ten portions; another report gives twenty-eight portions. Ten lots were cast and called azlam.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: كانوا يجزئونها عشرة أجزاء، عن أبي عمرو، وقيل: ثمانية وعشرين جزءا،

rows.speaker: الفراء والأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ and al-Akhfash analyze “month of Ramadan” as the predicate of an omitted subject, understood as “it is the month of Ramadan.”
rows.anchor: قال: شهر رمضان، عن الفراء والأخفش.

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi treats it as a nominative apposition to the passive subject of “fasting was prescribed upon you.”
rows.anchor: الثاني: على ما لم يسم فاعله بدلا من الصيام، كأنه قيل: كتب عليكم شهر رمضان، عن الكسائي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third nominative analysis makes “month of Ramadan” a subject whose predicate is “in which the Qur’an was sent down.”
rows.anchor: الثالث: الابتداء، وخبره الذي أنزل فيه القرآن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possible accusative analyses understand an imperative to fast Ramadan, make it an apposition to the numbered days, take it as an adverb according to al-Akhfash, or as an exhortation according to Abu ʿUbayda, like “God’s she-camel.”
rows.anchor: وفي نصبه وجوه: قيل: صوموا شهر رمضان، وقيل: بدلا من أيام معدودات.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ connects wa-li-tukmilū to an omitted clause: the ordinance was given so that you complete the count.
rows.anchor: قيل: عطف على جملة؛ لأن بعده محذوفا، كأنه قيل: ولتكملوا العدة شرع ذلك، عن الفراء،

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj instead connects it to an implied clause indicated by what precedes: God made things easy for you so that you complete the count.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على تأويل محذوف دل عليه ما تقدم أن يسهل عليكم ولتكملوا العدة، عن الزجاج.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda is accusative as a circumstantial expression: the Qur’an was sent down as guidance.
rows.anchor: نصب على الحال، كأنه قيل: أنزل فيه القرآن هاديا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase “on a journey” coordinates with “ill” because it has the same meaning as “a traveler”; compare 10:12, where several states coordinate with “on his side.”
rows.anchor: لأنه بمعنى الاسم، كأنه قيل: أو مسافرا، ومثله: (دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage next clarifies the time of fasting, its obligation, and the concession that applies to it.
rows.anchor: ثم بين تعالى وقت الصوم ووجوبه والرخصة فيه، فقال تعالى: (شهر رمضان)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense requires fighting as long as disbelief remains and therefore rules out taking jizya from Arab polytheists; there is agreement that jizya is taken from Magians, used as evidence for taking it from non-Arab polytheists, while al-Shafiʿi classifies Magians as scripturalists.
rows.anchor: من مشركي العرب جزية، وقد بينا ذلك، ولا خلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sacred month is so called because fighting and similar acts forbidden at other times are prohibited in it; hurumat are protected sanctities, and qisas is equal retaliation, doing the like of what was done.
rows.anchor: سمي الشهر حراما؛ لأنه يحرم فيه ما يحل في غيره من القتال ونحوه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The aggressor is a wrongdoer who exceeds the limit; ʿada and iʿtada may be synonymous, or the derived form may intensify the meaning.
rows.anchor: والمعتدي: الظالم المجاوز للحد، وعدا واعتدى قيل: بمعنى، كقرب واقترب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿa is a particle of accompaniment; here it means God’s support accompanies the pious.
rows.anchor: (مع): حرف المقارنة، ومعناه ههنا مصاحبة النصرة للمتقين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With no overt predicate for “the sacred month,” one analysis means that fighting in one sacred month is matched by fighting in another; another makes the second sacred month compensation for a missed pilgrimage the prior year.
rows.anchor: فيه قولان: الأول: قتال الشهر الحرام بقتال الشهر الحرام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is reported to concern the compensatory ʿUmra: Quraysh prevented the Prophet’s party from visiting in Dhul-Qaʿda 6 AH, then they returned for ʿUmra in Dhul-Qaʿda 7 AH under the treaty.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزلت الآية في عمرة القضاء، وذلك أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - خرج عام الحديبية للعمرة،

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو علي والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu ʿAli, and al-Zajjaj report that Quraysh asked Muhammad whether fighting in a sacred month was forbidden; after he said yes and they threatened to fight him, this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: فقال الحسن وأبو علي والزجاج: إن مشركي قريش قالوا: يا محمد، نهيت عن قتالنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation matches this sacred month, when the Muslims performed ʿUmra, with the month in which they had been turned back; another matches fighting in one sacred month with fighting in another.
rows.anchor: هذا الشهر الحرام الذي اعتمرتم فيه بالشهر الذي. صددتم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacred things balanced in retribution may be the sacred month, the sanctuary, and ihram; another view generalizes the rule to every violated sanctity.
rows.anchor: والحرمات قصاص في جمعه قولان، قيل: حرمة الشهر، وحرمة البلد، وحرمة الإحرام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Specific examples of reciprocal balance are entry into the sanctuary in ihram at the compensatory ʿUmra for the earlier exclusion, and fighting in a sacred month for the other side’s violation of sacred prohibitions.
rows.anchor: قيل: دخوله المسجد محرما في سنة القضاء قصاص لرده محرما في السنة الأولى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If someone wrongs you, respond in kind; the second use of “transgress” is not a real sin but verbal pairing, as in 42:40, “the requital of an evil is an evil like it.”
rows.anchor: والثاني ليس باعتداء، وإنما أتى به على مزاوجة الكلام، قال تعالى: (وجزاء سيئة سيئة)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view has pilgrims stop the talbiya after reaching Mina and casting the first pebble at the Jamrat al-ʿAqaba; Malik says a resident stops after standing at Arafat, after touching the Black Stone, or upon seeing the House.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك بن أنس: إذا وقف بعرفة فأما المقيم فيقطع التلبية إذا استلم الحجر، وقال مالك بن أنس: إذا رأى البيت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalaq is a share of good received according to entitlement; qadaʾ is settling a matter decisively and thoroughly, the root of the title qadi.
rows.anchor: الخلاق: النصيب من الخير على تقدير الاستحقاق. والقضاء: فصل الأمر على إحكام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashadda dhikran may be governed by the comparison ka- and put in the genitive, or by the verb udhkuru and put in the accusative.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان: أحدهما: الكاف فيكون موضعه جرا، والآخر الفعل في (اذكروا)

rows.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and others interpret the rites as the pilgrimage and the devotional acts commanded to pilgrims; Mujahid instead says they are sacrificial animals.
rows.anchor: قيل: حجكم، وما أمرتم به في التعبدات، عن الحسن وجماعة،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the rites as sacrificial animals.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الذبائح، عن مجاهد (فاذكروا الله) قيل: هذا يجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view makes remembering God obligatory after the rites are completed; another takes the command to apply while completing them.
rows.anchor: قيل: هذا يجب بعد قضاء المناسك، وقيل: مع قضاء المناسك، وتقديره:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance is glossed as takbir during the days at Mina because it is distinctive to those days, as all supplications, or as affirmation of divine unity and glorification, the latter reported from Abu Muslim.
rows.anchor: قيل: التكبير أيام منى؛ لأنه الذكر المختص في هذه الأيام، وقيل: سائر الأدعية،

rows.speaker: أنس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Anas, al-Hasan, and Qatada say people used to mention their fathers and boast of them forcefully; they should remember God at least as intensely, or more because of his blessings.
rows.anchor: أو أشد ذكرا لما له عليكم من النعمة، عن أنس والحسن وقتادة.

rows.speaker: عطاء والربيع والضحاك
rows.claim: ʿAta, al-Rabiʿ, and al-Dahhak compare invoking God for help with a child calling for his father.
rows.anchor: كذكر الصبي لأبيه، إذ قال: يا أبت في قول عطاء والربيع والضحاك.

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says not to forget the benefactor in any circumstance, just as one does not forget one’s parents.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا تنسوا المنعم في الأحوال كما لا تنسوا الآباء، عن أبي مسلم،

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli says people were habituated to repeated mention of their fathers, so they were ordered to remember God to that degree.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانوا يلهجون بذكر الآباء فأمر بذكره على هذا الحد، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aw can function like wa, while ashadda dhikran may mean more remembrance or better remembrance.
rows.anchor: يعني وأشد ذكرا، (أو) بمعنى الواو، وقيل: أكثر ذكرا، وقيل: أحسن ذكرا فمن الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some people ask only for worldly goods such as camels, sheep, and servants, and have no share in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أعطنا من أموال الدنيا إبلا وغنما وعبيدا ونحو ذلك وما له في الآخرة
